reason: A DFT/QTAIM analysis of CH...X hydrogen bonding and crystal packing in ionic cobalt(III) complexes; it shares only computational-chemistry method vocabulary with the asked-about radical-scavenging and ferrous-ion-binding study of a naphthoquinone.

Reports ethylene binding modes in Cu(I) pyridinophane complexes analysed by NBO and QTAIM; the only overlap with the question is the computational method acronym, not antioxidant capacity or ferrous-ion chelation by a natural product.

Studies how the Mycobacterium tuberculosis RD1 locus (ESAT-6/CFP-10) shapes human dendritic cell maturation and Th1 priming; same pathogen as background, but no rodent model, no hypoxic necrotic granulomas and no drug-regimen response.

Shows that affinity modulation of platelet alphaIIbbeta3 (GPIIb-IIIa) is an intrinsic property of the receptor, using antibody-induced activation in CHO cells and solubilised receptor. Same receptor and the same issue of changing ligand-binding strength, but measured as bulk binding rather than single-molecule force jumps during receptor clustering.

Describes FDA protocols for dominant lethal, host-mediated and in vivo cytogenetic mutagenicity testing of GRAS substances in rodents; related regulatory rodent safety testing, but not a three-month repeat-dose oral toxicity study of an aluminosilicate.

Reports that exon 16-disrupted haemophilia A mice of two strains develop functional neutralising anti-FVIII inhibitors after repeated recombinant FVIII treatment, with isotype and cytokine characterisation. That is exactly the rodent model of inhibitor-driven treatment resistance the question asks about.

Shows that liver-directed AAV gene therapy eradicates pre-existing anti-FVIII inhibitors in haemophilia A dogs; it uses an animal model of inhibitor-mediated treatment resistance, but in dogs and with a therapeutic rather than model-characterising aim.

A tetrode recording study of cortical dendritic membrane potential and dendritic spikes in freely behaving rats; it shares only the DMP abbreviation with the question about intracellular pH control of myocardial potassium efflux.

Examines calcium signalling and viability effects of 2,4-dimethylphenol in PC3 prostate cancer cells; the overlap is the abbreviation DMP, not cardiac potassium loss, perfused hearts or magnetic resonance measurement of intracellular acidity.

A disproportionality analysis of sex differences in fall-risk-increasing drugs in the FDA adverse event reporting system; pharmacovigilance signal detection, with nothing about neural population dynamics or low-dimensional functional organisation of brain activity.

Presents a deep-learning-assisted high-speed single-particle-tracking system that resolves the 3D orientation of anisotropic gold nanoparticles in living cells; same live-cell tracking field, but it solves orientation estimation under low signal-to-noise rather than globally optimal assignment of detections to individual fluorophore trajectories.

Shows that Gr-1 antibody depletion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells restores antitumour CD8 responses in murine hepatocellular carcinoma after EZH2 inhibition; it answers the MDSC-depletion question in the same cancer, but the immunosuppressive microenvironment arises from drug treatment rather than incomplete thermal ablation.

Describes a distributed multiagent architecture for a case-based reasoning system that adapts 3D numerical organ phantoms for radiation dosimetry; the only link to the question is the multiagent framing, with no transcript selection and no breast cancer cohort.

Analyses COL4A5 splicing abnormalities and genotype-phenotype correlation in X-linked Alport syndrome, including novel atypical splicing patterns beyond splice-consensus point mutations. Same collagen gene, same hereditary nephritis and the same aberrant mRNA processing mechanism, but not a report of a specific deep intronic variant.

Characterises the morphology and thermal degradation kinetics of bacterial nanocellulose produced by Gluconacetobacter xylinus; no keratinase activity, no feather or poultry waste substrate and no statistical design of experiments.

Reports a single-reaction multiplex PCR that simultaneously detects blaKPC, blaNDM, blaIMP and blaOXA-48-like (alongside mcr-1), validated against reference strains and 197 clinical Enterobacteriaceae. This is precisely the multiplex assay for carbapenemase genes in enteric isolates that was asked about.

Maps immunocytological PCNA distribution through early Xenopus laevis embryonic cell cycles and the midblastula transition; replication-machinery localisation, but in amphibian embryos entering rapid divisions rather than mammalian cells withdrawing from the cycle.

A pilot feasibility and accuracy study of sentinel node biopsy with dye and radiocolloid in breast cancer, reporting identification, sensitivity and false-negative rates; it evaluates the technique itself, not whether its introduction changed adherence to treatment guidelines.

Reports success and false-negative rates of sentinel node biopsy after neoadjuvant chemotherapy within NSABP B-27; performance of lymphatic mapping in a trial setting rather than any measure of guideline-concordant care for early-stage disease.

Compares FITC and GFP labelling for studying neutrophil phagocytosis of Bordetella pertussis and shows FITC impairs adenylate cyclase toxin; it concerns a respiratory pathogen and labelling artefacts, not enumeration or persistence of dominant Gram-positive taxa in human stool.

Shows PPAR-gamma activation by pioglitazone limits NLRP3-driven chondrocyte pyroptosis in osteoarthritic cartilage and a rat knee OA model; it shares the inflammasome sensor and joint inflammation, but involves no irradiation and no osteoclast differentiation factor.

Shows the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15d-PGJ2 blocks caspase-1 activation by the NLRP1 and NLRP3 inflammasomes in murine gout and anthrax models; inflammasome pharmacology as background, with no radiation exposure, arthritis scoring or RANKL measurement.

Analyses immunoglobulin VH gene family usage in human diffuse large-cell lymphoma (DLC) and follicular lymphoma; it shares only the DLC abbreviation with the question about immune gene diversity in captive versus free-living lemurs.

Generates dendritic-cell-like cells (DLC) in long-term mixed leucocyte culture and characterises their surface markers and allostimulatory function; a pure abbreviation collision with the Madagascan primate immunogenetics question.

Profiles expression of the DLC-1 and DLC-2 Rho-GAP tumour suppressor genes across human solid tumours; the DLC letters match but the subject is cancer gene expression, not MHC or immune gene diversity in wild and captive primates.

Compares morphologic subtypes of diffuse large cell lymphoma (DLC versus immunoblastic) for response and survival after CHOP-type chemotherapy; only the DLC acronym connects it to the question about lemur immune gene diversity.

Describes canine large granular lymphocyte leukaemia and a derived cell line named DLC 02 that releases infectious retroviral particles; the match is a cell-line label, not captive versus wild primate immunogenetics.
Reports that knockout of the DLC-1 (Arhgap7) Rho-GAP gene causes mid-gestation embryonic lethality in mice; mouse developmental genetics sharing only the DLC abbreviation with the question.

Shows diacylglycerol analogues open TRPC-like, second-messenger-operated calcium channels in mouse cortical neurons, with the responses explicitly not regulated by PKC; neuronal channel-modulation background, but no voltage-gated sodium channel phosphorylation and no antiepileptic drug block.

Demonstrates that PKC inhibits TRPC3 channels indirectly by stimulating PKG, mapping the relevant phosphorylation sites; it is PKC-dependent channel regulation, but on TRPC3 rather than sodium channels and with no drug blocking persistent current.

Tracks pH-dependent cellular uptake of dual-coloured fluorescent prototype foamy virus (PFV) particles; it shares the PFV abbreviation with pre-formed vesicles but concerns virus entry, not lipid nanoparticle manufacture or mRNA delivery to the retina.

Reviews Iranian traditional medicinal herbs used against Giardia infection; a gastrointestinal parasite and phytotherapy review that addresses neither coeliac disease nor Helicobacter pylori gastritis or its histology.

Examines how IGF-1 and CCL2 affect endothelial cell proliferation, fibronectin deposition, migration and tube formation; endothelial matrix biology as background, but it does not compare proteoglycan expression between quiescent and dividing primary cultures.

Synthesis, catecholase and phenoxazinone synthase activity and DFT-TDDFT study of Mn(III) and Cu(II) Schiff-base complexes; it shares only coordination-chemistry and DFT vocabulary with the question on uncatalysed amine addition to electron-poor metal alkynes.

Reports trimetallic Fe(III)/M(II) complexes whose bridging ligand arose by oxidative addition, focusing on electronic transitions and magnetic coupling; the shared word addition does not make it a mechanistic study of amine addition to electron-poor triple bonds.

Studies charge delocalisation, NIR transitions and electronic coupling in a cyclometalated bisruthenium complex with DFT/TDDFT support; organometallic electronic structure, not catalyst-free hydroamination mechanism, theory or applications.

Builds homology models of human CYP4A11 (and CYP2C9) and docks lauric acid to explain terminal versus non-terminal hydroxylation; same family of human haem monooxygenases, but the subject is regioselectivity and active-site architecture, not isoform differences in hydrogen peroxide produced by uncoupling.

Reviews OPG-L/ODF (RANKL) and osteoprotegerin as the paracrine pair that sets osteoclast formation; useful osteoclastogenesis background, but the inhibitory mechanism described is decoy-receptor sequestration of a TNF-family ligand, not a death-receptor ligand acting through a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor.

Reviews the OPG-RANK-RANKL triad in bone resorption, osteolysis and bone metastasis; relevant regulation-of-osteoclast-formation background with no death-receptor ligand and no p27-type CDK inhibitor mechanism.

Measures age-related decline of cell-mediated immunity in mice using splenocyte cytotoxicity and skin allograft rejection rates; allograft immunity background only, with no intestinal mucosa, villous architecture or hypersensitivity reaction in the small bowel.

Evaluates the hypoxic-cell radiosensitiser doranidazole in murine SCCVII tumours and human pancreatic xenografts; a radiation-modifier study in mouse tumour models, but it sensitises tumours rather than testing whether a nitroxide antioxidant spares normal tissue while leaving the tumour unprotected.

Characterises the anti-CD22 Pseudomonas exotoxin immunotoxin CAT-8015 in B-cell lines, a subcutaneous xenograft model and cross-species pharmacokinetics; the same class of targeted toxin, but no brain tumour and no comparison of bolus injection with pressure-driven (convection-enhanced) infusion.

Qualitative HPTN 083 sub-study of trial experiences, acceptability and adherence barriers for long-acting injectable cabotegravir PrEP at US and Brazilian sites; it addresses willingness to use injectable HIV prevention, but in cisgender MSM and transgender women rather than women in the United States and Africa.

Reports Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever seroprevalence of 3.0%, tick and animal-blood exposure risk factors and knowledge gaps in rural villages with known transmission. Same virus and the same seroprevalence-plus-exposure-risk design, but conducted in rural Georgia rather than a southern African population.

Reviews CCL7 chemokine biology in tumorigenesis, the tumour microenvironment and metastasis; chemokine-driven monocyte recruitment as background, with no pair of receptors governing blood monocyte trafficking and no experimental demyelinating disease model.

Uses a multiplex PCR to score combined GSTM1 and GSTT1 null genotypes in 233 Polish individuals and ties homozygous deletion to absent detoxifying enzyme activity; it supplies the multiplex assay and the genotype-to-detoxification link, though its own subject is population genotype distribution.

Reports a low-cost, reproducible high-throughput PCR assay for glutathione S-transferase polymorphic alleles, benchmarked against single nucleotide extension and applied to paediatric cancer risk; an assay for the same gene variants, but the linked phenotype is cancer risk and chemotherapy response rather than measured detoxification capacity.

A genotype-phenotype study of 84 patients with biallelic UNC13D mutations causing familial haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis type 3, covering presenting features, CNS involvement and mutation spectrum; same inherited hyperinflammatory syndrome, but no stem cell transplantation outcomes and no virus-driven lymphoproliferation.

Tests trimethoprim-sulfadoxine against Escherichia coli in subcutaneous tissue cages in calves, with plasma and tissue-cage fluid concentrations and bacterial counts; veterinary pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic work, but a different drug class, a different species and an efficacy rather than oral disposition endpoint.

Describes abortive infection, transformation and genetic change of B77 avian sarcoma virus in rat embryo cells; the same virus system as background, but nothing on spliced viral mRNA accumulation or methyl-donor depletion in avian cells.

Reports Sendai-virus-mediated rescue of B77 Rous sarcoma virus from transformed rat cells by fusion with chicken cells; avian sarcoma virus biology as background, with no analysis of viral mRNA splicing, stability or methylation.

Clones and sequences Rous sarcoma virus cDNAs spanning the env and src splice junctions, defining the common donor and the two acceptor sites of the spliced viral mRNAs. It establishes the identity and structure of the spliced RSV transcripts central to the question, but does not examine their accumulation under methyl-donor depletion.

Compares regulation and signalling of the class A scavenger receptors SR-AI/II and MARCO in mouse peritoneal macrophages, including IL-12 output and opsonin-independent phagocytosis; macrophage receptor biology rather than antigen presentation to lymphocytes by isolated guinea-pig liver macrophages.

Shows impaired LPS/IFN-gamma-driven tumoricidal activation of peritoneal macrophages in mammary-tumour-bearing mice together with reduced T-cell IFN-gamma production; macrophage-lymphocyte cooperation as background, but not hepatic resident macrophage antigen presentation in guinea pigs.
A cancer registry report of incidence and mortality trends in New South Wales for 1997; population epidemiology with no drug distribution, tumour tissue penetration or platinum chemistry of any kind.

Genomic and transcriptomic analysis of a Staphylococcus aureus small colony variant from a relapsed prosthetic joint infection, where the phenotypic switch coincided with loss of a 42.5 kb prophage alongside an rpoB deletion. It links phage content to phenotypic switching in a chronic, biofilm-associated infection, but does not test phage-driven switching during biofilm formation itself.

Describes archaeal community composition and diversity with depth across seven Pacific Ocean water columns by 16S pyrosequencing; marine microbial diversity background, but not metabolic breadth in hot, geochemically dynamic seafloor sediments.

Shows that melanoma cells from lymph node metastases adhere to lymph node vitronectin through integrin alphavbeta3, blocked by RGD peptide and LM609; the same integrin and an adhesion-receptor mapping design, but a different cell type and a matrix ligand that is not a secreted immediate-early gene product.

A phase II multicentre trial of donor-derived cytokine-induced killer cells given with unmanipulated DLI to patients relapsing after allogeneic transplant, reporting toxicity and antitumour activity. The same cytokine-activated lymphocyte product in relapsed haematological malignancy, but allogeneic rather than autologous, later-phase and not confined to lymphoma.

Shows a phosphorus-containing dendrimer drives human monocytes toward an alternative, IL-10-associated immunosuppressive phenotype that inhibits CD4 T-cell proliferation; monocyte activation-state background, but the trigger is a synthetic nanomaterial and dendritic cell commitment is not the endpoint.

Compares stimulatory and inhibitory maturation of GM-CSF/IL-4-derived human myeloid dendritic cells and shows endogenous IL-10 renders them suppressive; related IL-10 and DC differentiation biology, but it does not test blockade of monocyte-to-dendritic-cell conversion with redirection toward macrophages.

Shows the PRMT5 inhibitor DW14800 suppresses liver cancer stem cell self-renewal and restores hepatocyte differentiation via HNF4alpha transcription in HCC cells and xenografts. A concrete therapeutic strategy against hepatic tumour-initiating cells, though it covers one target rather than surveying their roles and the range of targeting approaches.

Reviews how climate change alters distribution, seasonality and socioeconomic burden of arthropod-borne diseases, contrasting surveillance and control capacity in resource-rich countries with Afghanistan and other low- and middle-income settings. It brings climatic, environmental and socioeconomic drivers together, though framed as a regional climate-impact review rather than a weighting of their relative contributions.

Presents SOPRA, which selects satisfiable mate-pair constraints by statistical optimisation to scaffold contigs in de novo assembly of short reads; same assembly goal using paired reads, but it links contigs rather than merging overlapping read pairs into longer single fragments.

Shows probiotics combined with Salvia miltiorrhiza polysaccharide lower hepatic triglyceride and cholesterol while modulating gut microbiota and improving insulin resistance in high-fat-diet NAFLD mice. It supports the intestinal-bacteria contribution to hepatic fat accumulation in insulin-resistant mice, but through an intervention rather than small-molecule metabolite profiling.

Quantifies accumulated LC3-positive autophagic vesicles, altered lysosomal markers and colocalisation of hyperphosphorylated tau with LC3 in post-mortem cortex from familial Alzheimer disease, corticobasal degeneration and progressive supranuclear palsy patients. The paper's subject is exactly autophagic vesicle formation and impaired clearance in neurons and its link to degenerative dementia pathology.

Shows autophagy activation and enhanced mitophagy in Purkinje cells of pcd mice before neuronal death, with BAX-independent loss excluding classic apoptosis; it addresses autophagic vesicle formation and turnover in neurons, but in a cerebellar degeneration model rather than dementia pathology.

Provides a structural and dynamic model of how GDI recognises geranylgeranylated Rab5-GDP at the endosomal membrane and holds it soluble in the cytosol. It covers the dissociation-inhibitor arm of small GTPase regulation for one Rab, but not the exchange factor or GTPase-activating components the question also names.

Identifies class A scavenger receptor as a receptor for dendritic cell nibbling of membrane from live cells and shows SR-A-dependent cross-presentation of gp100 to MHC class I-restricted T cells, contrasting it with CD36-mediated apoptotic uptake. Receptor-dependent antigen capture plus cross-presentation to cytotoxic T cells, but from live rather than dying cells.

Compares phagocytosis of apoptotic and necrotic K562 leukaemia cells by human blood CD11c+ DC, plasmacytoid DC and immature monocyte-derived DC, implicating CD36 together with CD91 and CD11c in the uptake. It answers the dying-cell receptor part of the question, but does not test presentation of the acquired antigen to cytotoxic lymphocytes.

Shows the heat shock protein gp96 matures human dendritic cells and that its uptake receptor is downregulated on mature DC; related cross-priming and DC receptor biology, but the antigen source is a chaperone-peptide complex, not dying cells engulfed through two surface receptors.

Describes cytokine-driven in vitro differentiation of CD34+ progenitors into Birbeck-granule-positive Langerhans cells and interdigitating dendritic cells with differing antigen uptake and presentation markers; dendritic cell ontogeny background rather than receptor-mediated engulfment of apoptotic cells and priming of cytotoxic T cells.

Identifies NF90 as an influenza A NS1-interacting host factor that relieves NS1-mediated suppression of PKR phosphorylation and stress granule formation. It documents one specific function of the nonstructural protein NS1, its innate-immune antagonism, rather than surveying the protein's many roles.

Reports that influenza A and B M2 proteins bind Hsp40 and p58IPK and enhance PKR autophosphorylation; same virus and the same PKR pathway, but M2 is a structural ion channel protein rather than the nonstructural protein the question is about.

Reviews anthocyanin structural diversity, pathway genes, WD40-bHLH-MYB regulation and metabolic engineering in Arabidopsis thaliana. It covers biosynthesis and biotechnological manipulation of a major class of plant polyphenols, but is confined to one model species and says little about their biological roles.

Characterises Arabidopsis abi1, abi2 and abi3 mutants and the overlapping subsets of ABA responses each gene controls; plant water-stress signalling genetics as background, with no reanalysis of existing photosynthesis data and no inference of metabolic relationships.
